sources.basis: Management plan, Figure 81 description and written building history. Minaret north-west, small northern court, western raised yard and a western gate. 1939 work introduced pointed arches and alhor stone façade covering and stairs around the original minaret.
The sacred western gate was reinstalled on 19 September 2016. The gate is reached by the courtyard associated with the historic burials.
Documents the former burial enclosure as the large western court, a small northern courtyard giving access to the minaret, and the building’s long history of remodelling.
UNESCO’s restoration account describes a three-aisled mosque, a repaired flat roof and courtyard walls, and the reconstruction of one door leaf from recovered timber.

cartographicEvidence: The rounded eastern projection is the mihrab. The attached unnamed way shares the northwestern boundary across two near-perpendicular faces. Model its enclosure as a partly open northwestern wing, with its use and internal divisions estimated.
